clue.text: Grumbling that one may be found unattractive in the future

indicators.note: in shows that one word is set inside the other, the plain one found within the future one

parts.note: the coming years are the years in the future, so the future gives coming
plain means unattractive in looks

explanation.surface: Someone moaning that a person might turn ugly in years to come.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAIN goes inside COMING, splitting it after COM; 'that one may be found' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling and moaning both describe voicing discontent, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cash put noisily in boxes

indicators.note: noisily says the phrase must be heard spoken rather than read as written

parts.note: to cough up is to pay, so cash put in is coughs in

explanation.surface: Money is dropped with a clatter into containers.
explanation.walkthrough: COUGHS IN, said out loud, matches the plural of the burial box; coughing up is informal for paying money over.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffins are the long wooden cases that hold the dead, a particular kind of container.

clue.text: Makes the acquaintance of proper skinhead

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of skin

explanation.surface: Someone is introduced to a respectable skinhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is split: 'head' picks the first letter of 'skin'. MEET for proper is an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be introduced to someone for the first time is to get to know them, a straight equivalent.

clue.text: It's ridiculous to go about without one!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'It's ridiculous to go about without one!', gives 'ridiculous' as definition but no wordplay that builds LUDICROUS; likely garbled OCR, and a search of the exact text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: It's ridiculous to go about without one!

clue.text: Terrible man with only one vehicle

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A dreadful fellow owns just a single car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like an adjective; it points to Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the sixteenth-century tsar of Russia, known by that epithet.

clue.text: Thought provoking notion I have under Tory leader

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the following piece sits below the one before it

parts.note: an idea is a notion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Tory

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A concept of mine sits beneath a Conservative party head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts IVE below T in the down light; IDEA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideative describes something relating to or forming ideas, so prompting thought.

clue.text: A letter from Greece must finally jog mama in some way or another

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word jog
this phrase says the letters of mama are arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone must eventually nudge their mother into action somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' is a link; the final G of 'jog' is followed by AMMA, mama rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Very old worker found drinking nice cocktail

indicators.note: drinking means one piece takes the other inside, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of nice are mixed up

explanation.surface: An elderly labourer is discovered having a pleasant mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts NCIE (an anagram of NICE, signalled by 'cocktail') inside ANT; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, extremely aged.

clue.text: Bad, drawn out, ill-timed

indicators.note: bad here signals that the letters are put into a faulty, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A list of complaints about something poor, lengthy and badly timed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like the definition, but it is the anagram signal; the definition is 'ill-timed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfortunate or inconvenient, as with an event happening at the wrong moment.

clue.text: Meadow providing food for the bird

parts.note: a meadow is a field
fare is food, as in a menu's fare

explanation.surface: A grassy field supplies food for the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a species of thrush, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: The fellow in charge is crazy

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: The man running things has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means wildly excited or frenzied, close to mad.

clue.text: Vet lost a penny to the small creature

indicators.note: lost means a piece is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: to vet something is to inspect it
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An animal doctor misplaced a coin given to a tiny animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like a noun for an animal doctor; it is the verb meaning to examine.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are tiny six-legged animals, so a small creature.

clue.text: Toasters cook things in layers

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so cook signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kitchen toasters prepare items stacked up in tiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'things' is a link joining the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratose is a botanical term meaning arranged in strata, that is in tiers.

clue.text: Device to detect snores perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of snores might be in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A gadget that picks up the sound of someone snoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is an instrument that responds to and registers a physical stimulus.

clue.text: Put forward the name of disorganised middle eastern nation

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters given are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East or Middle Eastern

explanation.surface: Propose the name of a chaotic Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: ME (Middle Eastern) and NATION are mixed together as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to propose them formally as a candidate.

clue.text: Position of director is not very clear

definitions.meaning: a director stands in charge, above the actors of a play or film
said of the sky when clouds cover it and the day is dull

explanation.surface: Where the director stands is a bit murky.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer as two words: a director is set over the players.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded over and grey, hence dim rather than bright.

clue.text: Agent on edge, and being given a telling off

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece is placed above the next

parts.note: a rep, a representative, is a sales agent
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A nervous sales agent is being scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous, but it splits into a placing word and RIM; 'being given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprimand is a formal rebuke, a scolding.

clue.text: Nothing follows brilliant bird

indicators.note: follows means the O comes after the word for brilliant

parts.note: flaming means blazing or brilliantly bright
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing comes after a dazzling bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading species with long legs and neck.

clue.text: Came round untidy silo where an item of clothing was found

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the other piece
untidy says the letters of silo are in a messy order

explanation.surface: Someone visited a messy grain store and found a garment there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts ISOL (an anagram of SILO, signalled by 'untidy') inside CAME; 'where ... was found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: Sea food for bird and man

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
Les is a man's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: Seafood suitable both for a bird and a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles are small edible shellfish gathered from beaches.

clue.text: Suit provided for digging the garden

definitions.meaning: one of the four sets in a pack of playing cards
tools with a flat blade used to turn soil

explanation.surface: A card set offered for turning over the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are both a card suit and the long-handled tools gardeners dig with.

clue.text: Hitch for orthopaedic surgeon to handle

definitions.meaning: a hitch is a snag that holds progress up
a bone surgeon might deal with a spine that needs putting right

explanation.surface: A problem passed to a bone doctor to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as SET BACK, to fix a spine in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal or check to progress, much like a snag.

clue.text: Study the paperwork to ensure it is appropriate

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
forms are official papers to fill in

explanation.surface: Read the documents to make sure everything is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ensure it' is a link; CON for study is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with rules or standards, to be fitting.

clue.text: Monsters trample gorse

indicators.note: to trample something is to crush it out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Giant beasts stomp all over the prickly shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, a kind of monster.

clue.text: Those who are gifted move more than they should

definitions.text: Those who are gifted move more than they should

indicators.note: move signals that the letters of gifted shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Talented people tend to be restless and wriggle too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those who are' is a link; the whole clue doubles as a description of a restless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person who keeps squirming is called by this name, as is the action.

clue.text: Performance backed by the Italian singer

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance

indicators.note: backed means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A show supported by an Italian vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian singer' looks like one phrase, but 'the Italian' gives IL; Beniamino Gigli was a famous Italian tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated operatic tenor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Hey you! I've had an after thought on the way

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to share a thought they had while out walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've had an' and 'on the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This whispered sound is used to catch someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Dead right, after the event!

parts.note: the late someone is someone dead

explanation.surface: Someone says something is lifeless, correctly, once it is all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, once something has happened.

clue.text: Lost again in sentiment

indicators.note: in here hints that the letters of the words before it are in disorder

explanation.surface: Losing out once more prompts wistful feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LOST AGAIN are rearranged; the clue relies on 'Lost' to suggest disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful sentimental longing for the past.

clue.text: Noticed that a man took pudding

parts.note: spotted means noticed
Dick is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone saw a man take a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'took' are links. SPOTTED DICK is a traditional British steamed suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a classic British dessert of suet sponge dotted with dried fruit.
